Based on the search results, here's what I found about the macOS security update in August 2026 that is being actively exploited:

## The Vulnerability

CVE-2026-65400 is a critical authentication issue impacting the Screen Sharing component that could allow an attacker already on the network to authenticate to the built-in remote desktop feature service without valid credentials. It has a CVSS score of 9.8.

## The Patch

The shortcoming was addressed as part of an emergency update in macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, and macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 earlier this month. Apple released an advisory on August 6, 2026.

## Active Exploitation

A recently patched security flaw in Apple macOS has come under active exploitation in the wild to deploy a cryptocurrency miner, the Netherlands National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC-NL) has warned. The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC-NL) reported on August 12 that attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-65400, an authentication bypass in macOS Screen Sharing, to compromise Macs with port 5900 exposed to the Internet. In every case reported to the agency, attackers obtained root access and installed a Monero cryptocurrency miner.

CVE-2026-65400 is being actively exploited in the wild, prompting its addition to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on August 18, 2026.

## Mitigation

Users are encouraged to update to the latest version as quickly as possible: macOS Tahoe 26.x: Upgrade to version 26.6.1 or later. macOS Sequoia 15.x: Upgrade to version 15.7.9 or later. macOS Sonoma 14.x: Upgrade to version 14.8.9 or later.

# macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 Security Update Summary

**Release Date:** August 17, 2026

**Affected System:** macOS Tahoe

**Number of Vulnerabilities:** 30 CVEs addressed

## Key Vulnerabilities

**Critical Issues:**
- ImageIO arbitrary code execution (CVE-2026-65346): "An integer overflow was addressed with improved input validation."
- IOGPUFamily memory corruption (CVE-2026-64788): Affects web content processing
- Multiple WebKit vulnerabilities enabling Safari crashes and memory corruption

**Notable Kernel Issues:**
- Use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-65343) allowing remote system termination
- Out-of-bounds read (CVE-2026-65349) potentially exposing kernel memory

**WebKit Component:** Received the most patches (18 CVEs), primarily addressing maliciously crafted web content processing

## Exploitation Status

The document contains no statements regarding active exploitation in the wild or Apple's awareness of real-world attacks.

## Additional Context

This update delivers fixes originally introduced in macOS Golden Gate 27 beta, indicating these vulnerabilities were being addressed across multiple OS versions.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about CVE-2026-65400:

## Overview

CVE-2026-65400 is a pre-authentication vulnerability in the macOS Screen Sharing daemon (screensharingd) that lets a network attacker authenticate without valid credentials and gain root-level remote code execution.

## CISA KEV Catalog Status

Apple patched the flaw on August 6, 2026, in macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, Sequoia 15.7.9, and Sonoma 14.8.9, but after reports of active exploitation, CISA rescored it from 7.1 to 9.8 (Critical) on August 14 and added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on August 18, giving federal agencies until August 21, 2026 to remediate.

## Active Exploitation

The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC-NL) reported on August 12 that attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-65400, an authentication bypass in macOS Screen Sharing, to compromise Macs with port 5900 exposed to the Internet. In every case reported to the agency, attackers obtained root access and installed a Monero cryptocurrency miner.

## Technical Details

CVE-2026-65400, the more serious of the two, exploits a flaw in the Screen Sharing service's implementation of Secure Remote Password (SRP), which ultimately allows pre-authenticated remote code execution on all supported macOS versions.

Based on the search results, I found information about Safari 26.6.1 security content from August 18, 2026.

Safari 26.6.1 was released August 18, 2026 and is available for macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia. The update addressed an out-of-bounds access issue that could lead to an unexpected Safari crash when processing maliciously crafted web content.

The security advisory includes multiple CVE vulnerabilities that were addressed in this release. Some of the key CVEs mentioned include:

- CVE-2026-64784, which involved an out-of-bounds access issue addressed with improved bounds checking
- CVE-2026-43795
- CVE-2026-65338

The update addressed various types of security issues including memory handling improvements, input validation enhancements, and memory corruption fixes through better state management and locking mechanisms. You can view the complete list of CVEs and detailed descriptions on the official Apple Support page for Safari 26.6.1.

Short answer

**Two things are competing for "most recent," depending on what counts as a macOS security update:**

| Release | Date | Available

for |
|---|---|---|
| **macOS Tahoe 26.6.2** — most recent macOS *OS* update | 17 Aug 2026 | macOS Tahoe only |
| **Safari 26.6.1** — most recent security release *

affecting macOS* | 18 Aug 2026 | macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia |

**Apple identifies no actively exploited issues in either one.** ([Apple security

releases](https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100))

---

## macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 (17 Aug 2026)

- Every entry on the advisory carries the line
"Available for: macOS Tahoe" — so this update targets Tahoe only. Sequoia and Sonoma did **not** get a same-day OS counterpart
; their most recent OS updates remain 15.7.9 and 14.8.9 from 6 Aug ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281), [release

list](https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100)).
- It fixes roughly 30 CVEs, the largest cluster (~18) in WebKit, plus ImageIO (
CVE-2026-65346, integer overflow → arbitrary code execution), IOGPUFamily (CVE-2026-64788), and Kernel issues CVE-2026-65343 (
use-after-free) and CVE-2026-65349 (out-of-bounds read). *Caveat: I read this advisory through a page-summarizing fetch rather than transcribing it line by line,
so treat the exact count and the completeness of this CVE list as approximate — the advisory itself is authoritative* ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281

)).
- **The page contains no "exploited," "exploitation," or "Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited" language** — Apple's standard formula

for in-the-wild attacks is absent ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281)).

## The actively exploited issue — and why it is *not* Apple identifying it

There **

is** an actively exploited macOS flaw right now, but the exploitation finding does not come from Apple:

- **CVE-2026-65400**, Screen Sharing: "An att
acker on the network may be able to authenticate to Screen Sharing without valid credentials." Fixed via improved state management; credited to Alf
redo Pesoli (@\_\_rev) via Bynario Atlas. Patched **6 Aug 2026** in **

macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, and macOS Sonoma 14.8.9** ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148170)).
- Apple's advisory for it

**also carries no exploitation notice** ([Apple](https://support.apple.com/en-us/148170)).
- Exploitation was reported externally: NCSC-NL war
ned on 12 Aug that attackers are hitting Macs with port 5900 exposed to the internet, gaining root and installing a Monero miner; CISA r
escored the bug from 7.1 to 9.8 on 14 Aug and added it to the KEV catalog on 18 Aug with a 21 Aug federal remediation deadline ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.
com/2026/08/apple-macos-screen-sharing-flaw.html), [Help Net Security](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/08/17/apple-macos-screen-sharing-flaw/), [Tom's Hardware](https://www.t
omshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/macos-screen-sharing-flaw-exploited-to-root-macs-and-plant-monero-miners), [Malwarebytes](https://www.malwar

ebytes.com/blog/bugs/2026/08/update-your-mac-screen-sharing-vulnerability-exploited-in-the-wild)).

So the prec

ise answer to your question as asked: **Apple identifies zero actively exploited issues in its most recent macOS security update.** The one macOS vulnerability known to be under attack was already patched eleven days earlier, and

its exploited status was established by NCSC-NL and CISA rather than by Apple.

## Fact vs. inference vs. uncertainty

- **Supported fact:** release dates, "Available for" sc

oping, CVE-2026-65400's description and credit, absence of exploitation language on Apple's pages, KEV addition.
- **Inference (mine):** that
Sequoia/Sonoma were deliberately left at 15.7.9/14.8.9 for the 26.6.2 content — I infer this from the release list showing no

17 Aug counterpart for them; Apple does not explain the split, and one could still ship later.
- **Disagreement in s
ources:** the CVSS score for CVE-2026-65400 moved 7.1 → 9.8; that is a CISA rescoring, not two
sources contradicting each other, but you'll see both numbers in circulation ([Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/macos-screen-
sharing-flaw-exploited-to-root-macs-and-plant-monero-miners)). One secondary write-up characterizes the flaw as pre-auth **remote root code execution** via a
Secure Remote Password implementation bug, which is stronger than Apple's own wording of "authenticate without valid credentials" ([Huntress](https://www.huntress.com

/blog/macos-screen-sharing-rce-patched)).
- **Weak evidence:** a related second Screen Sharing CVE (CVE-2026-43760) appears in third

-party analysis; I did not verify it against an Apple advisory, so don't rely on it.
- **Not established:** whether Apple will retro

actively annotate advisory 148170 with an exploitation note, as it has done occasionally in the past. As of today it has not.

**Practical upshot:** Tahoe users should be on 26.6.2; Sequoia/
Sonoma users need 15.7.9 / 14.8.9 for the exploited Screen Sharing bug plus Safari 26.6.1. If Screen Sharing/VNC (port 5900) is reach
able from the internet on any unpatched Mac, treat that as urgent.
